title: docs(skills): objectstack-ai names what replaces the retired agent keys; eval case 6 grades the permission name
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DLCo5F2y7fgbM8tstGoyyUn)_

Fixes #37419

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：靠这份 AI 技能文档工作的助手，遇到已下线的两个智能体配置项时，能说出该改用哪两个配置项、工具该登记在哪里；评测里「用脚本批量批准待办」那道题改为检查权限名，不再因换说法或中文回答被误判。
- 为什么做：技能评测跟进项。第 5 题带技能原本 0/5，补了两行文档后 4/5；第 6 题按您选的方案 A 改题后 5/5，不带技能 0/5，本轮达标。
- 出错会怎样：只改文档两行、示例删一行、评测题一行，运行行为不变；撤回这一个改动即可恢复。
- 要你做什么：技能文档属受管文件，合并需要 os-zhuang 批准。

## What changes

- `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, the retired-keys table (2 rows): the `agent.tools` row now says where the tools go (a `defineSkill` under the stack's `skills`); the `agent.knowledge` row names the two keys that restrict retrieval on the knowledge source (`aiExposed`, `source.where`). Both come from the saved phase-2 patch, applied by hand on current `main`.
- `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, the skill example: one sample instruction line removed ("Escalated cases must summarise the actions already taken."). This is the whole payment for the two rows: with the rows alone the file measured 6813 tokens against its 6801 ceiling (over by 12); with the line gone it measures 6797. The other trims of the saved patch (a sample tier, `active: true`, two tightened sentences) are not applied: the ratchet does not need them.
- The human-in-the-loop paragraph is not touched: it reads exactly as on `main` (ruling 7208935788, execution item 2).
- `skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json`, case 6: `must_contain` becomes `ai:approve` alone. `must_not_contain`, the prompt and `expected_output` are unchanged.
- `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: the ceiling row for `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` is lowered from 6801 to 6797, the file's measurement on this head merged with `main` (`9ce0cca9`). `main` now reds a row left above its measurement, so the 4 tokens the trim over-paid are banked in the row. A lowering, not a raise; no other row moves.
- `.changeset/37419-ai-skill-tombstone-replacements.md`: `@objectstack/skills` patch.
- Head `9ce0cca9` is `86f70f00` plus a merge of `main` (`44ccf94a`) and the row. `git diff 86f70f00 9ce0cca9 -- skills/` is empty: the skills tree is byte-identical to the head the acceptance round ran on.

### Why case 6 changed

Its two tokens (`signed-in session`, `refused`) were English prose. The grader matches a token as a literal, case-sensitive substring and normalises nothing (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/grade.ts`, docblock: "the tokens are code spellings"), so a correct answer that paraphrased ("while signed in", "refuses") or came back in Chinese was marked wrong. Two rewordings of the skill paragraph did not move the rate (2/5, 1/5, 3/5 with the skill). `ai:approve` is a code spelling the skill teaches in the same paragraph, and it reads the same in any answer language. The card's rule admits a case change only for wording the skill rightly does not use; the maintainer's ruling 7208935788 (option A, 「A 改题，改查代码写法」) extends it to this reason. Known limit, accepted in the analysis (7207740184): the token pins "the answer used the skill's approval paragraph", not the whole answer; the forbidden approve call stays the case's real guard.

### Skills size readings

| reading | before (`main` `44ccf94a`) | after (`9ce0cca9`) |
|---|---|---|
| `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, lines | 485 | 484 |
| `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, tokens of ceiling (ratchet) | 6801 of 6801 | 6797 of 6797 |
| all `skills/*/SKILL.md`, lines | 4960 | 4959 |
| authored bundle, tokens of ceilings (ratchet) | 199710 of 199710 | 199706 of 199706 |
| whole shipped tree, tokens | 301276 | 301268 |

Net lines across `skills/**`: +3 / -4 = -1 (budget: at most +3).

## Tests

Acceptance round (ruling execution item 4), run on head `86f70f00` (the current head `9ce0cca9` has the same skills tree, byte for byte), 5 draws per arm, cases 5 and 6. Scratch worktree at the pushed head, eval file trimmed locally to ids 5 and 6 (uncommitted); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios skill-evals --skills objectstack-ai --repeats 5`. Driver: claude-code-cli 2.1.332, subscription login, the login's default tier, CLI default effort, `--max-turns 16`, 2 at once. 20 of 20 turns ran; none invalid or errored.

| case | with skill | no skill | tokens missed (with skill) | bar | met |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 4/5 | 0/5 | `surface`, `aiExposed` (1 draw) | with skill at least 4/5 | yes |
| 6 | 5/5 | 0/5 | none | with skill at least 4/5; no skill at most 1/5 | yes |

Regrade of the surviving `main` recordings (item 3; a figure, not acceptance): the phase-1 round on `579b8577`, case 6 against `ai:approve` with the forbidden call unchanged: with skill 4/5, no skill 0/5 (it was 2/5 and 0/5 against the two phrases). Counted by hand with the grader's own rule (literal substring), because the runner's `--regrade` sets a case whose tokens changed since the round apart and does not regrade it; run on a copy, it printed "1 case(s) changed since the round, set apart: not regraded". The same count on the two later local rounds gives 5/5 and 4/5 with the skill, 0/5 and 0/5 without, which matches the fork report.

No behaviour pinned by a unit test changed, so no ablation.

## Acceptance notes

- Case 5's one miss is a single draw lacking `surface` and `aiExposed`; the earlier rounds on the same two rows also read 4/5.
- `overlap-check --branch=claude/area-o1B-37419` at `9ce0cca9`: `main` and three open PRs merge cleanly, one is reported (below). Two open PRs (37676, 37661) share `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` and merge cleanly by text. The row is pinned at the measurement (headroom 0), so whichever of the three lands later re-measures the ratchet on the merged text. PR 37676 also shares `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` and merges cleanly. PR 36158 is reported as conflicting in that script; its head conflicts with `main` in the same file without this branch, so the conflict is not this PR's.
- The runner's `--regrade` cannot answer "what would the old answers score under the new tokens" for a changed case; that is its declared design (case hash), noted here and not filed.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:
1. `skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json`, case 6 `must_contain`: one line, the ruled change.
2. `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, the two rows of the retired-keys table: check `aiExposed` and `source.where` against the knowledge-source table higher in the same file.
3. `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, the skill example: one instruction line gone, nothing else.

Two-minute check: `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`; expect exit 0 and the line "skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md is 6797 tokens (ceiling 6797; headroom 0)".

<details><summary>Local gates at 9ce0cca9</summary>

- `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: exit 0, "skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md is 6797 tokens (ceiling 6797; headroom 0)" and "61 authored bundle file(s) within their ceilings". Before the row moved, the same merged tree was red: "its ratchet ceiling is 6801, above the measurement by 4".
- `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs --self-test`: exit 0, "111 cases pass".
- `packages/spec/scripts/platform-catalog.test.ts` (the test that names the ratchet script): 20 of 20 pass.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 67 derived (the script edit adds 18 families). 63 ran, all exit 0. 4 exit 3, NOT MEASURED, each refusing for want of a full workspace build: `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`. CI runs them; the first, third and fourth were exit 0 at `86f70f00`, and the delta touches no package.
- `dispatch-gates --ran`: "67 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 63 run, 4 NOT-MEASURED (4 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)".
- At `86f70f00` (skills tree unchanged since): `check:skill-examples` exit 0, "352 prose examples type-check across 3 surface(s)"; `skill-evals --dry-run` exit 0.

</details>
